newsitem.title: FRANCE: French defence ministry gets budget specialist.
newsitem.headline: French defence ministry gets budget specialist.

text.p: Alain Richard, a Socialist expert in state budgeting, was appointed defence minister in France's new left-wing cabinet on Wednesday.

Richard, 51, is little known outside parliamentary circles but both Socialist and rival centre-right colleagues say he was a particularly effective rapporteur (secretary) of the National Assembly's budget committee in 1988-1993.
Like his predecessor as defence minister, conservative Charles Millon, he has no apparent experience in defence affairs.

Millon, who launched President Jacques Chirac's wide-ranging reforms to abolish conscription and build all-professional armed forces, was considered a competent administrator by the defence establishment despite his lack of knowledge of military affairs.

Richard graduated from the elite Ecole Nationale d'Administration civil service school and holds degrees in public law and political science. He began his professional career in the Council of State, France's top administrative court in 1971.
As a student in 1962, he joined the small left-wing United Socialist Party (PSU) of Michel Rocard, who became his political mentor.

He joined the mainstream Socialist party in 1975, at a time when Rocard was unsuccessfully challenging the late Francois Mitterrand for the leadership and he became a member of the party's decision-making executive in 1988.
Rocard was prime minister from 1988 to 1991 during Mitterrand's presidency from 1981 to 1995.
Richard was first elected to the National Assembly in 1978 as representative of the Val d'Oise area north of Paris, a mix of high-rise working class suburbs and rural villages.
He also served as vice-president of the assembly's laws committee, being actively involved in studying problems of local administration.
Defeated in the 1993 elections to the National Assembly, he was elected to the Senate (upper house) in 1995 and sits on its finance commission.
